description: Opening scene establishing a detective protagonist and crime scene. Tests continuity setup, voice, and pacing.

sceneBrief.title: The Body in the Garden
sceneBrief.emotionalGoal: Unease and curiosity — the reader should feel the tension of discovery and the weight of an unusual death
sceneBrief.payoff: Establishes that the victim was researching a cold case when they died, setting the central mystery
sceneBrief.tension: Moderate — professional discovery scene with undercurrent of wrongness

draft:
The garden stretched out behind the Rosethorn estate like a held breath. Dew clung to the grass, heavy and cold, and the first grey light of dawn did nothing to warm it. Detective Sarah Chen stepped over the yellow tape and ducked under a low-hanging branch, her shoes soaking through in three paces.

'Over here, Detective.'

Officer Mike Ramirez stood near the fountain, his notebook out, his face the colour of old paper. He had been on the force eighteen years. Sarah had never seen him pale before.

She crossed the lawn. The body lay half-in, half-out of the fountain — a woman in her sixties, grey hair spread like roots in the water, one hand still gripping a leather-bound notebook. The water had stained the pages dark, but the cover was dry. Sarah crouched, careful not to touch anything.

'ID?'

'Dr. Eleanor Vance. She was the estate's historian. Lived in the gatehouse.' Ramirez flipped a page. 'Neighbour called it in at 5:12 AM. Said she heard a splash and then nothing.'

'A splash at five in the morning?'

'That's what I thought.'

Sarah studied the body. No visible trauma. No blood. The expression on the dead woman's face was not fear — it was surprise. As if she had been mid-thought when something interrupted her permanently.

'Get me the medical examiner,' she said. 'And check what Dr. Vance was working on. If she was the estate historian, there's got to be an office, a study, something.'

Ramirez nodded and stepped away to make the call. Sarah remained by the fountain, her eyes fixed on the notebook clutched in the dead woman's hand. The cover had gold lettering, barely legible through the water damage. She tilted her head.

'Rosethorn: A Complete History,' she read aloud. The title meant nothing. But the fact that a historian had died clutching her own research meant everything.

Sarah stood and looked at the manor beyond the garden. Its windows were dark, its gables sharp against the lightening sky. Somewhere in that building was whatever Eleanor Vance had found. And somebody had wanted it to stay buried.
storyBible:
Character: Detective Sarah Chen
Role: Protagonist / Lead Detective
Goal: Solve the murder of Dr. Eleanor Vance and uncover the truth behind a cold case
Voice: Direct, observant, dry humour under pressure, methodical
Notes: Transferred from Homicide to Cold Case six months ago after a personal tragedy; carries guilt she masks with procedure
Traits: thorough, intuitive, guarded, stubborn

Character: Officer Mike Ramirez
Role: Uniformed first responder
Goal: Support the investigation and keep scene secure
Voice: Professional, slightly deferential, genuinely affected by the work
Notes: 18-year veteran who has developed a protective instinct toward his partners; notices details others miss because he watches people, not evidence
Traits: observant, loyal, empathetic, steady

Character: Dr. Eleanor Vance
Role: Victim / Estate Historian
Goal: Was researching the Rosethorn family cold case
Voice: (deceased — described through her work as precise and passionate)
Notes: Retired university archivist who took the gatehouse position three years ago; was known in academic circles for her meticulous research into local history
Traits: meticulous, private, determined

Location: Rosethorn Estate Garden
Description: Formal English garden behind a Gothic-revival manor, centred on a stone fountain; overgrown in places, suggesting reduced maintenance in recent years
Notes: The fountain has been in the family for generations; the garden was once the pride of the estate but has fallen into slight disrepair
Traits: secluded, layered, history-heavy
